name: com.malimoney/calculators
title: MaliMoney Calculators
description: 30+ tested personal-finance calculators: retirement odds, Roth, Social Security, debt, FIRE.

tools.name: roth_conversion_one_year
tools.description: Evaluate the tax cost and bracket/IRMAA impact of converting a given amount from traditional IRA/401(k) to Roth in a single year. Use when the user asks 'should I do a Roth conversion', 'how much can I convert without bumping a bracket', 'what would converting $X cost in taxes', or wants a single-year Roth conversion analysis. Pass either conversionAmount OR fillBracketTo (not both). Returns an educational tax estimate, not advice — tell the user to confirm with a CPA before converting.

fillBracketTo.description: Alternative: compute the conversion amount that exactly fills the user's current bracket up to this rate's ceiling.

year.description: Tax year. Defaults to current year.

userAge.description: Age used to gate IRMAA analysis (applies at 63+).

tools.name: retirement_readiness
tools.description: Quick on-track / tight / behind check for retirement. Use when user asks 'am I on track', 'can I retire', 'how am I doing for retirement', or wants a one-shot readiness score. Returns status, reasoning, and the single highest-leverage fix.

retirementTaxRatePct.description: Effective tax rate % on retirement withdrawals — set this (e.g. 15-25 for traditional-IRA-heavy savers) for an after-tax grade instead of the optimistic tax-free default.

tools.name: monte_carlo_retirement
tools.description: Stress-test the retirement plan across thousands of randomized market paths. Returns success rate WITH a 95% confidence interval, ending-balance percentiles, worst drawdown, and CVaR (average ending balance of the worst 5% of paths). Use when the user asks 'what are the odds', 'what's my success rate', 'what if markets crash', or wants a probability-based retirement analysis. For crash / bad-timing / sequence-of-returns questions set returnModel='block_bootstrap' (resamples real market history — fat tails + bad-streak clustering — more realistic than the default normal model). Quote the success rate with its CI, and cite CVaR for 'how bad could it get'.

returnModel.description: Return model. Default 'normal'. Use 'block_bootstrap' for crash/sequence-of-returns questions; 'student_t' for parametric fat tails.

tools.name: mortgage_payoff_what_if
tools.description: Model mortgage payoff scenarios — extra monthly principal, lump sum, or refinance. Use when the user asks 'should I pay off my house', 'extra principal vs invest', 'when will my mortgage be done', 'refi vs stay'. Pass balance + annualRatePct + monthsRemaining.

annualRatePct.description: Current annual interest rate as percent (e.g. 6.5).

monthlyPayment.description: Current P+I monthly payment. Derived from balance/rate/term if omitted.

extraMonthly.description: Extra principal payment per month (extra_monthly scenario).

lumpSum.description: One-time lump sum applied immediately (lump_sum scenario).

refiClosingCost.description: Refi closing cost; factored into break-even (refi scenario).

refiTermMonths.description: New term length in months (refi scenario).

tools.name: ss_claim_age
tools.description: Find the optimal Social Security claiming age. Use when the user asks 'when should I claim Social Security', 'should I wait until 70', or wants SS optimization. Pass PIA (monthly benefit at FRA) — prompt the user for it from their ssa.gov statement if unknown.

pia.description: Primary Insurance Amount — monthly benefit at FRA, from SSA statement.

fraAge.description: Full retirement age (66-67 depending on birth year).

spousePia.description: Optional: spouse's PIA. Joint optimization not yet modelled — flagged as note.

tools.name: withdrawal_order
tools.description: Model tax-efficient retirement withdrawals year-by-year across taxable, traditional, and Roth accounts. Use when the user asks 'which account should I tap first', 'how do I withdraw efficiently', or wants a retirement income strategy. Handles RMDs at 73+. Returns an educational projection, not advice — the user should confirm a withdrawal strategy with a CPA/advisor.

annualNeed.description: Today's-dollars annual spending in retirement; inflated internally.

taxableCostBasis.description: Cost basis of the taxable account. When provided, only the gain above basis is taxed on each taxable withdrawal (instead of the whole pull) — pass it when known for a more accurate tax estimate.

traditionalBalance.description: Traditional IRA/401(k) balance subject to ordinary income tax on withdrawal.

tools.name: longevity_estimate
tools.description: Actuarial life-expectancy and planning-horizon estimate from mortality tables. Use for 'how long should I plan for', 'what age should I plan to', 'how long does my money need to last', or any retirement-horizon question — instead of assuming age 95. Pass partnerAge for couples: it returns the LAST-survivor horizon (the age by which there's only a ~10% chance either partner is alive), which is what a joint plan must fund. Quote the planning-horizon age; for couples explain they should fund the last survivor, not the average.

partnerAge.description: Partner's age — include for couples to get joint last-survivor figures.

tools.name: optimal_spend
tools.description: Solve for the MOST the user can sustainably spend per year in retirement while keeping a target probability (default 85%) that the money lasts. Use when the user asks 'how much can I spend', 'what's a safe withdrawal', 'how much can I afford in retirement', or 'what's the most I can take out'. Unlike a projection you feed a spend into, this SOLVES for the spend number via simulation over realistic historical market paths. Quote the annual and monthly figure and the target success rate; present it as an educational estimate, not advice.

targetSuccessRate.description: Desired probability the plan lasts, 0.5–0.99. Default 0.85.

tools.name: hsa_contribution
tools.description: How much HSA contribution room the user has left for 2026 and the tax savings of using it. Use when the user asks 'how much can I put in my HSA', 'am I maxing my HSA', or about HSA limits/catch-up. 2026 limits: $4,400 self-only, $8,750 family, +$1,000 catch-up at 55+. Pass coverageType + age; optionally ytdContribution and marginalRatePct for the tax-savings estimate.

marginalRatePct.description: Marginal federal rate % for the income-tax-savings estimate.

tools.name: backdoor_roth
tools.description: Apply the IRS pro-rata rule to a backdoor Roth (traditional→Roth conversion). Use when the user asks 'is my backdoor Roth tax-free', 'what's the pro-rata rule on my conversion', or has pre-tax IRA money alongside nondeductible contributions. The rule aggregates ALL traditional/SEP/SIMPLE IRAs: tax-free share = basis ÷ (basis + pre-tax). Pass conversionAmount, afterTaxBasis (nondeductible contributions), and pretaxBalance (total pre-tax IRA balance); optionally marginalRatePct.

conversionAmount.description: Amount being converted to Roth this year.

afterTaxBasis.description: Total nondeductible (after-tax) contributions across all IRAs — your basis.

pretaxBalance.description: Total pre-tax balance across all traditional/SEP/SIMPLE IRAs.

marginalRatePct.description: Marginal federal rate % for the tax-cost estimate.

tools.name: inherited_ira_rmd
tools.description: Required minimum distribution / deadline rules for an IRA the user INHERITED (post-SECURE-Act, deaths 2020+). Use when the user asks 'what's the RMD on an IRA I inherited', 'when do I have to empty an inherited IRA', '10-year rule', or about inherited/beneficiary IRA distributions. Pass beneficiaryType, beneficiaryAge, inheritedBalance, ownerDeathYear, and ownerHadStartedRMDs (true if the original owner had begun their own RMDs). Returns the applicable rule, first-year RMD, and empty-by deadline. Educational — inherited-IRA rules are nuanced; tell the user to confirm with a CPA.

beneficiaryType.description: spouse; eligible designated beneficiary (minor child of owner, disabled/chronically ill, or <10yr younger); non_eligible (most adult children → 10-year rule); entity (estate/charity).

beneficiaryAge.description: Beneficiary's current age (drives the Single Life divisor).

inheritedBalance.description: Current balance of the inherited IRA.

ownerHadStartedRMDs.description: True if the owner died on/after their Required Beginning Date (had started their own RMDs).

tools.name: college_savings
tools.description: Project a 529 / college-savings plan and tell the user if they're on track + how much to save. Use when the user asks 'are we saving enough for college', 'how much should I put in a 529', 'will my 529 cover college'. Projects the plan to college start, then draws it down against the inflated TOTAL cost of attendance. Pass childAge, currentBalance, monthlyContribution, and schoolType (in_state_public/out_of_state_public/private benchmarks ~$30k/$49k/$63k) or customAnnualCost. Returns projected value, total cost, coverage %, gap, and required monthly to fully fund. Educational — costs/returns vary.

schoolType.description: Benchmark total cost of attendance; use 'custom' with customAnnualCost for a specific school.

customAnnualCost.description: Today's total annual cost of attendance (when schoolType=custom).

tools.name: life_insurance_need
tools.description: Estimate how much life insurance a person/family needs using the capital-needs (DIME) method. Use when the user asks 'how much life insurance do I need', 'are we covered if something happens to me', 'do we have enough life insurance'. Recommended coverage = income replacement (present value of annualIncome × replacement% for incomeReplacementYears at a real return) + mortgage + other debts + final expenses + education fund, less existing earmarked savings and any existing coverage. Pass annualIncome (required) plus whatever else is known. Returns the gross-need breakdown, recommended total face amount, additional coverage needed beyond an existing policy, and an adequacy verdict. Educational — survivor benefits and individual circumstances vary.

annualIncome.description: Insured person's annual income to (partly) replace.

incomeReplacementYears.description: Years of income to replace (e.g. until kids are independent or spouse retires).

realReturnPct.description: Real (after-inflation) return used to present-value the income stream.

otherDebts.description: Other debts to clear (auto, student, credit card).

educationFund.description: Lump sum to fund children's education.

existingSavings.description: Liquid assets earmarked to support survivors.

tools.name: pension_lump_sum
tools.description: Compare a one-time pension lump sum against keeping the monthly pension (annuity). Use when the user asks 'should I take the lump sum or the pension', 'is my pension buyout a good deal', 'lump sum vs monthly pension'. Present-values the pension stream (monthlyPension×12, optional COLA) over the payout horizon (lifeExpectancyAge − currentAge) at a discount rate, then compares to the lump sum; also returns the implied payout rate and the break-even return the lump sum must earn to match the pension. Pass lumpSum and monthlyPension (required). Single-life model — note it doesn't separately value joint-survivor benefits. Educational.

lifeExpectancyAge.description: Age through which payments are assumed to last.

discountRatePct.description: Rate used to present-value the pension (e.g. a safe return you could earn on the lump sum).

colaPct.description: Annual cost-of-living adjustment on the pension, if any.

tools.name: charitable_giving
tools.description: Compare charitable-giving tax strategies — give annually vs bunch several years into one (donor-advised fund) vs a Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD) from an IRA — and recommend the best after-tax option. Use when the user asks 'what's the best way to give to charity', 'should I bunch my donations', 'is a QCD or donor-advised fund better', 'how much do I save in taxes by donating'. Pass annualDonation and marginalRatePct (required); filingStatus and otherItemizedDeductions sharpen the standard-vs-itemized comparison, and age enables the QCD option (70½+). Returns each strategy's annual tax benefit and the recommendation. Federal-only educational estimate.

filingStatus.description: Filing status (drives the standard deduction). Default married.

otherItemizedDeductions.description: Non-charitable itemized deductions (SALT, mortgage interest, etc.). Default 0.

bunchYears.description: How many years of giving to bunch into one for the bunching strategy.

age.description: Age — enables the QCD strategy when 70½+.

tools.name: divorce_impact
tools.description: Model the financial impact of a divorce or separation: how assets and debts would split, each spouse's post-divorce monthly budget and immediate net worth, a simple multi-year net-worth trajectory for each, and a ballpark one-time legal-cost estimate by route (DIY, mediation, litigation). Use only when the user is going through, seriously considering, or explicitly asks to model a divorce or separation ('what would divorce look like financially', 'could I afford my own place if we split up', 'how would we split things') — never bring this up unprompted. Manual-inputs only: pass each spouse's monthly take-home income, combined shared monthly expenses, and combined marital assets/debts (required), plus the assumed split (default 50/50). Alimony is a simple manual override (a monthly amount + who pays) — this tool does NOT apply state guideline formulas. Present results in a measured, calm, supportive tone — this is emotionally difficult territory, never funny, roasting, or glib, and never take a side or imply blame. Always pair the numbers with the returned disclaimer: an educational estimate, not legal or financial advice — recommend a family-law attorney, mediator, or CPA for real decisions.

spouseALabel.description: Display name for spouse A, e.g. 'You'. Default 'Spouse A'.

spouseBLabel.description: Display name for spouse B. Default 'Spouse B'.

combinedMonthlyExpenses.description: Combined shared monthly household expenses today.

maritalAssets.description: Combined marital assets subject to division.

maritalDebts.description: Combined marital debts subject to division. Default 0.

assetSplitPctToA.description: Percent of marital assets (after legal costs) going to spouse A.

debtSplitPctToA.description: Percent of marital debts going to spouse A. Defaults to assetSplitPctToA.

expenseSplitPctToA.description: Percent of ongoing shared expenses (groceries, kids, insurance) spouse A carries post-split.

movingSpouse.description: Which spouse(s) take on a new monthly housing cost.

newMonthlyHousingCost.description: New monthly housing payment for the moving spouse(s).

legalRoute.description: Divorce process route, drives the legal-cost ballpark.

legalCostOverride.description: User-supplied total legal cost, overriding the ballpark table.

projectionYears.description: Years to project each spouse's post-split net worth.

netWorthGrowthPct.description: Blended annual growth/shrink rate applied to each spouse's post-split net worth.

tools.name: auto_loan
tools.description: Calculates an auto loan's financed amount and monthly payment, accounting for sales tax, down payment, and trade-in value. Use when estimating vehicle financing costs.

vehiclePrice.description: Vehicle purchase price in dollars; defaults to 0.

downPayment.description: Cash down payment in dollars; defaults to 0.

tradeInValue.description: Trade-in value in dollars, deducted from the taxable price and financed amount; defaults to 0.

salesTaxPct.description: Sales tax percentage, expressed as 7 for 7%, not 0.07; defaults to 0.

aprPct.description: Annual percentage rate, expressed as 7 for 7%, not 0.07; defaults to 7.

loanTermMonths.description: Loan term in months, rounded to a whole month with a minimum of 1; defaults to 60.

tools.name: cd_hysa_growth
tools.description: Projects savings growth from a starting balance and monthly contributions using an effective APY. Use when estimating CD or high-yield savings account growth.

principal.description: Starting savings balance in dollars; defaults to 0.

monthlyContribution.description: Contribution in dollars at the end of each month; defaults to 0.

apyPct.description: Effective annual percentage yield, expressed as 4.5 for 4.5%, not 0.045; defaults to 4.5.

years.description: Savings horizon in years, converted to a rounded number of months; defaults to 0.

tools.name: coast_fire
tools.description: Estimates how much must be invested today to grow to a retirement target without further contributions. Use to assess Coast FIRE readiness given retirement spending, age, return, and withdrawal assumptions.

currentAge.description: Current age in years; defaults to 0.

retireAge.description: Planned retirement age in years; defaults to 65.

currentInvested.description: Current invested balance in dollars; defaults to 0.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected annual investment return percentage, expressed as 7 for 7%, not 0.07; defaults to 7.

annualRetirementSpend.description: Expected annual retirement spending in dollars; defaults to 0.

withdrawalRate.description: Annual withdrawal percentage, expressed as 4 for 4%, not 0.04; defaults to 4, with a minimum of 0.1 and a zero value treated as 4.

tools.name: compound_interest
tools.description: Projects the future value of a starting balance and monthly contributions with monthly compounding. Use to estimate investment growth over a specified time horizon.

principal.description: Starting invested balance in dollars; defaults to 0.

monthlyContribution.description: Contribution in dollars at the end of each month; defaults to 0.

annualRatePct.description: Annual return percentage divided by 12 for monthly compounding, expressed as 7 for 7%, not 0.07; defaults to 7.

years.description: Investment horizon in years, converted to a rounded number of months; defaults to 0.

tools.name: credit_card_payoff
tools.description: Estimates the payoff time, total interest, and total payments for a credit card balance with a fixed monthly payment. Use to evaluate a repayment plan or identify a payment that cannot cover monthly interest.

balance.description: Outstanding credit card balance in dollars; defaults to 0.

annualRatePct.description: Credit card APR percentage, expressed as 22 for 22%, not 0.22; defaults to 22.

monthlyPayment.description: Fixed monthly payment in dollars; defaults to 0.

tools.name: emergency_fund
tools.description: Calculates an emergency savings target, current expense coverage, and remaining funding gap. Use to plan an emergency fund and estimate funding time from monthly contributions.

monthlyExpenses.description: Monthly expenses in dollars; defaults to 0.

monthsOfCoverage.description: Desired number of months of expense coverage; defaults to 6.

currentSavings.description: Current emergency savings in dollars; defaults to 0.

monthlyContribution.description: Monthly contribution toward emergency savings in dollars; defaults to 0.

tools.name: fire_number
tools.description: Calculates a financial independence portfolio target, progress toward it, and estimated years to reach it. Use when planning retirement based on annual spending, contributions, investment returns, and a withdrawal rate.

annualSpending.description: Annual spending to fund from the portfolio in dollars; defaults to 0.

withdrawalRate.description: Annual withdrawal percentage, expressed as 4 for 4%, not 0.04; defaults to 4, with a minimum of 0.1 and a zero value treated as 4.

currentInvested.description: Current invested balance in dollars; defaults to 0.

annualContribution.description: Annual investment contribution in dollars; defaults to 0.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected annual investment return percentage, expressed as 7 for 7%, not 0.07; defaults to 7.

tools.name: growth_401k
tools.description: Projects 401(k) balance growth from employee contributions, employer matching, investment returns, and salary growth. Use to estimate retirement savings under different contribution and matching assumptions.

currentBalance.description: Current 401(k) balance in dollars; defaults to 0.

annualSalary.description: Starting annual salary in dollars; defaults to 0.

contributionPct.description: Employee contribution as a percentage of salary, expressed as 10 for 10%, not 0.10; defaults to 10.

employerMatchPct.description: Employer match as a percentage of the employee deferral, expressed as 50 for a 50% match, not 0.50; defaults to 50.

employerMatchLimitPct.description: Salary percentage up to which employee deferrals are eligible for matching, expressed as 6 for 6%, not 0.06; defaults to 6.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected annual investment return percentage, expressed as 7 for 7%, not 0.07; defaults to 7.

years.description: Projection horizon in years; defaults to 0.

salaryGrowthPct.description: Annual salary growth percentage, expressed as 3 for 3%, not 0.03; defaults to 0.

tools.name: home_affordability
tools.description: Estimates an affordable home price using income, existing debts, down payment, and housing costs. Use when assessing a home purchase budget under the calculator's affordability assumptions.

annualIncome.description: Gross annual income in dollars; defaults to 0.

monthlyDebts.description: Existing monthly debt payments in dollars; defaults to 0.

downPayment.description: Available down payment in dollars; defaults to 0.

mortgageRatePct.description: Annual mortgage interest percentage, expressed as 6.5 for 6.5%, not 0.065; defaults to 6.5.

loanTermYears.description: Mortgage term in years, with a minimum of 1; defaults to 30, and a zero value is treated as 30.

propertyTaxPct.description: Annual property tax as a percentage of home value, expressed as 1.1 for 1.1%, not 0.011; defaults to 1.1.

homeInsuranceAnnual.description: Annual homeowners insurance cost in dollars; defaults to 1500.

hoaMonthly.description: Monthly homeowners association dues in dollars; defaults to 0.

tools.name: inflation
tools.description: Calculates an amount's future cost, future purchasing power in today's dollars, and cumulative inflation. Use to understand how inflation changes prices and buying power over time.

amount.description: Dollar amount whose future cost and purchasing power are evaluated; defaults to 0.

years.description: Time horizon in years; defaults to 0.

inflationRatePct.description: Annual inflation percentage, expressed as 3 for 3%, not 0.03; defaults to 3.

tools.name: net_worth
tools.description: Calculates total assets, total debt, and net worth from asset and liability balances. Use to summarize a person's current financial position.

cash.description: Cash and cash account balances in dollars; defaults to 0.

investments.description: Investment asset value in dollars; defaults to 0.

homeValue.description: Home market value in dollars before subtracting mortgage debt; defaults to 0.

otherAssets.description: Other asset value in dollars; defaults to 0.

mortgageBalance.description: Outstanding mortgage debt in dollars; defaults to 0.

studentLoans.description: Outstanding student loan debt in dollars; defaults to 0.

creditCardDebt.description: Outstanding credit card debt in dollars; defaults to 0.

otherDebts.description: Other outstanding debt in dollars; defaults to 0.

tools.name: rent_vs_buy
tools.description: Compares the financial outcomes of renting and buying over a planned stay using housing costs, appreciation, and investment assumptions. Use when evaluating whether a home purchase makes financial sense relative to renting.

homePrice.description: Home purchase price in dollars; defaults to 0.

downPaymentPct.description: Down payment as a percentage of home price, expressed as 20 for 20%, not 0.20; defaults to 20 and is limited to 0–100.

mortgageRatePct.description: Annual mortgage interest percentage, expressed as 6.5 for 6.5%, not 0.065; defaults to 6.5.

loanTermYears.description: Mortgage term in years, with a minimum of 1; defaults to 30, and a zero value is treated as 30.

monthlyRent.description: Starting monthly rent in dollars; defaults to 0.

yearsStaying.description: Planned length of stay in years; defaults to 7.

homeAppreciationPct.description: Annual home value appreciation percentage, expressed as 3 for 3%, not 0.03; defaults to 3.

rentInflationPct.description: Annual rent increase percentage, expressed as 3 for 3%, not 0.03; defaults to 3.

investmentReturnPct.description: Annual return percentage on invested savings, expressed as 6 for 6%, not 0.06; defaults to 6.

propertyTaxPct.description: Annual property tax as a percentage of home value, expressed as 1 for 1%, not 0.01.

maintenancePct.description: Annual maintenance cost as a percentage of home value, expressed as 1 for 1%, not 0.01.

insurancePct.description: Annual homeowners insurance cost as a percentage of home value, expressed as 0.5 for 0.5%, not 0.005.

buyingCostPct.description: Buying transaction costs as a percentage of home purchase price, expressed as 3 for 3%, not 0.03.

sellingCostPct.description: Selling transaction costs as a percentage of home sale price, expressed as 6 for 6%, not 0.06.

tools.name: rmd
tools.description: Estimates an own-account required minimum distribution using age and the prior year-end balance with the IRS Uniform Lifetime divisor table. Use for the calculator's age-73-and-older RMD scenario.

age.description: Account owner's age in years, rounded down to a whole year; defaults to 0, with table lookup capped at age 120.

accountBalance.description: Retirement account balance in dollars as of December 31 of the prior year; defaults to 0.

tools.name: roth_vs_traditional
tools.description: Compares projected after-tax Roth and traditional retirement contribution values, including investing the traditional contribution's upfront tax savings. Use to assess how current and retirement tax rates affect the comparison.

contribution.description: Contribution amount in dollars; defaults to 0.

currentTaxRatePct.description: Current tax percentage applied to the contribution's upfront deduction, expressed as 24 for 24%, not 0.24; defaults to 24 and is limited to 0–100.

retirementTaxRatePct.description: Retirement withdrawal tax percentage, expressed as 22 for 22%, not 0.22; defaults to 22 and is limited to 0–100.

years.description: Investment horizon in years; defaults to 0.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected annual investment return percentage, expressed as 7 for 7%, not 0.07; defaults to 7.

tools.name: savings_goal
tools.description: Calculates the monthly contribution needed to reach a savings target, accounting for growth of existing savings. Use to plan contributions for a goal with a specified deadline and expected return.

goalAmount.description: Target savings balance in dollars; defaults to 0.

currentSaved.description: Current savings toward the goal in dollars; defaults to 0.

years.description: Time until the goal in years, converted to a rounded number of months; defaults to 0.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected annual return percentage divided by 12 for monthly compounding, expressed as 5 for 5%, not 0.05; defaults to 5.
